headline: Gold prices rise by ৳2,216; 22K gold now ৳2,24,182 per bhori
summary: The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) has increased gold prices after two consecutive rounds of reductions.
details: The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) has decided to increase the price of gold in the domestic market. The price of one bhori of 22-carat gold has been increased by ৳2,216, bringing the new price to ৳2,24,182.

According to a notice issued by BAJUS on Thursday (July 2), the new prices became effective from 10:00 AM that day. The decision was made unanimously by the BAJUS Standing Committee on Pricing and Price Monitoring after considering the overall situation.
The new price for 22-carat gold is ৳2,24,182 per bhori. For 21-carat gold, the price is ৳2,14,093, while 18-carat gold is ৳1,83,883 and traditional method gold is ৳1,50,232 per bhori.

BAJUS stated that these prices will remain in effect across all jewelry establishments until further notice. While wages may vary based on the design of the jewelry, the VAT is already included in the sale price, meaning no separate VAT can be collected from customers.

headline: 72,000 buildings in Dhaka could collapse in magnitude 7 earthquake
summary: Experts warn of a massive humanitarian disaster as the number of earthquakes in Bangladesh has risen significantly over the last 18 months.
details: A survey by the Integrated Disaster Management Program indicates that a magnitude 7 earthquake could cause 72,000 buildings in Dhaka to collapse. Experts warn that ruptured gas lines could further turn the capital into a fire zone, creating a secondary disaster.

According to the Meteorological Department, 52 earthquakes have hit Bangladesh in the last 18 months, with 39 originating within the country. These quakes ranged from 2.5 to 5.7 on the Richter scale, with the highest frequency occurring in Sylhet, Narsingdi, and Rangpur.

Rubaiyat Kabir, an official from the Earthquake Observation Center, noted that the average number of annual earthquakes within Bangladesh had been less than 10 between 2015 and 2021, but has increased significantly in recent years.

Professor Dr. Mehedi Ahmed Ansari of BUET warns that about 60% of the area under RAJUK's jurisdiction is built on soft or filled soil, increasing the risk. He noted that most of the 600,000 multi-story buildings in the city were constructed without following building codes.

Experts emphasize the need for structural reinforcement of existing buildings and the need for trained volunteers, as government manpower alone would be insufficient to handle the scale of a major collapse.

Since earthquakes cannot be predicted in advance, specialists stress that the only way to reduce losses is through rigorous preparation and ensuring the construction of earthquake-resistant buildings.
